In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 4G POCTs are more sensitive than the 3G POCTs in detecting HIV infection in the first 6 months after HIV infection.
the 4G POCT has a high sensitivity in chronic infection but a lower sensitivity in primary HIV-1 infection.
the 4th generation test has a sensitivity of 98% in chronic HIV infection and that the specificity is greater than 99.5% (99.8%) in the first and second generation test.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
4G tests are useful in primary care, but that they are not as good as laboratory tests.
the fourth generation HIV tests are more sensitive in the early stages of infection, but less so in chronic infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 4th generation tests are not a panacea for early HIV diagnosis, and the current 4th generation test (OraQuick) does not perform as well as the current standard of care (4th generation ELISA), especially in the first week of infection.
the fourth-generation assay is a valuable addition to the diagnostic armamentarium of HIV infection, and it is especially useful in the acute and early stages of HIV infection.
HIV-1 RNA is the most sensitive marker of HIV-1 infection and that the p24 antigen assay has limited utility in the diagnosis and management of HIV-1.
